sections.content: A closing thesis often combines several structures from this unit in one sentence — a relative clause, a ni... ni... sino contrast, a chain of passive participles — to state a considered judgment rather than just list facts. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Todas las naciones son comunidades imaginadas; ese hecho no las hace menos reales para quienes las viven y las defienden.
items.english: All nations are imagined communities; that fact doesn't make them any less real for those who live in and defend them.

items.spanish: El nacionalismo debe estudiarse ni como una verdad eterna ni como una simple mentira, sino como un proceso histórico concreto.
items.english: Nationalism should be studied neither as an eternal truth nor as a simple lie, but as a concrete historical process.

items.spanish: Recorrimos varias piezas de ese proceso: una bandera improvisada, un himno elegido por concurso, y fronteras que dividieron a comunidades enteras.
items.english: We covered several pieces of that process: an improvised flag, an anthem chosen by competition, and borders that divided entire communities.

items.spanish: Comprendido así, el nacionalismo deja de ser un simple telón de fondo y se convierte en uno de los proyectos más ambiciosos del periodo.
items.english: Understood this way, nationalism stops being a mere backdrop and becomes one of the era's most ambitious projects.

sections.content: Ni... ni... sino... is the structure for rejecting two extremes at once before proposing a third position — useful whenever an argument's real point is "it's neither of the easy answers, but this more complicated one instead."
